title: Learning symmetric juntas

problem.name: Learning symmetric juntas
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} An unknown $S\subseteq[n]$ has known even size $k$. Query access is to $f_S(x)=[\sum_{i\in S}x_i=k/2]$. Recover $S$ with bounded error; each query can specify a superposition of $n$-bit inputs.

\textbf{Learning a majority junta.} An unknown $S\subseteq[n]$ of known size $k$ defines $f_S(x)=[\sum_{i\in S}x_i\ge k/2]$, with the paper's tie convention. Given membership queries, recover $S$.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} $\Theta(k^{1/4})$ queries by Belovs' adversary-bound algorithm, with efficient implementations described in the subsequent symmetric-junta learning work.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Learning a majority junta.} $O(k^{1/4})$ queries by Belovs' symmetric-junta adversary algorithm; time-efficient variants incur additional logarithmic and input-description factors.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} $\Omega(k\log(n/k))$ classical binary queries by information theory for $k\le n/2$; finite-class elimination provides a general upper bound and active learning exploits the symmetric predicate.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Learning a majority junta.} $\Omega(k\log(n/k))$ classical binary queries for $k\le n/2$, by distinguishing the $\binom nk$ candidate supports.
